To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the structural dimension of the disambiguities can be used to automatically resolve ambiguities.

the disambiguate process can be characterized according to 10 dimensions (ontological dimensions, disambiguation dimensions and disambiguation solution dimensions), and the structural dimension can be applied to disambiguate ambiguities in the ontology alignment.
we present an ontology alignment disambiguating system that is based on the structural dimensions of the ontologies.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(i) the characterization of the disam- biguation scenarios according to their dimensions; (ii) the characterization of disambiguation strategies; (iii) the identification of disambiguated correspondences; and (iv) the automatic adoption of structural resolution strategies.
(a) identifying the disambiguing scenarios; and (b) proposing the adoption of the structural disambiguation of the ontology alignments.

the following contributions: 1) a systematization of ontology alignment disambiguity, 2) a proposal of the Ontological Structural Dimension to characterize the ontology matching scenarios, and 3) a proposal of a method to identify and automatically adopt structural disambiguation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
structural resolution of ambiguigity is not a solution for the majority of ambiguigities.
the proposed method is able to disambiguate 100% of the ambiguities in the test set, with an accuracy of 99% in the disambiguated correspondences.
the proposed approach is able to automatically resolve 90.5 % of ambiguities in 0.5 seconds on average.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a method for disambiguation of ontology correspondences based on structural resolution of ambiguigities.
we propose a method to identify the structural dimension of the ontology alignments, and then we apply the structural resolution to the disambiguations of the alignments.
we have proposed a new approach for the disambiguated ontology alignment, which is based on the structural dimension and on the ontology structural analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
disambiguation is not a single task, and that the disambigualion actions must be selected according to the scenario in which the disambigulation is performed.
disambiguation can be done automatically by means of structural analysis of ontologies, without the need to rely on external resources.
we have developed the first disambiguation system that automatically identifies the ambiguities and resolves them based on the ontology structure.
